approved_scope.title: Record relayed human decisions on approvals and reviews as claims, not authentication
approved_scope.description: Record relayed human decisions on approvals and reviews as claims, not authentication
acceptance_criteria: A record missing one of those details is refused before anything is written, and the refusal says which detail is missing.
A review an agent records for a person can carry the same record, shown the same way.
An approval tells me it matches the content it approved and nothing more; the name on it is a claim, not proof of who gave it.
That record is optional, so a person approving at their own terminal is not asked for one.
The change's status shows it beside the approval or review it belongs to.
The status says plainly that the record is a claim too, not proof that the person decided.
When an agent records a decision a person made somewhere else, I can see who decided, their exact words, where they said it, and which agent wrote it down.

answers.constraints: change.3md 'Release review: claims and authentication': names and provider declarations are claims, authentication is separately enforced policy; this change states that for approvals too and adds no authentication. sdd_version.rs forward-compat note: ScopedReviewRecord is a digest preimage, so per Leif ('Keep it out', 2026-11-05 20:19 MST via orc t18) relayed_by is left out of the review digest and records without it keep their exact bytes. Shared shape with Chough (ch-d7, chough#123), approved by Leif: relayed_by {decided_by, words, where, recorded_by}, all required, non-blank, <=4096 bytes, unknown keys refused, absent not null. A relay record never satisfies, clears or replaces a gate. Never weaken a gate, bound or test.
